questions.question: In generative AI, there is a specific concept used to represent words, sub-words, or characters that the model processes as discrete units of text. What is this concept called?

options.text: Vectors

explanation.summary: Vectors represent numerical embeddings rather than discrete text units.
explanation.why: Vectors are mathematical representations of data in multidimensional space and are commonly used after tokenization to encode semantic meaning. However, they are not the discrete text units processed directly from raw input text.
explanation.comparison: Tokens are discrete text units, while vectors are numerical representations derived from tokens.

options.text: Tokens

explanation.summary: Tokens are discrete units of text processed by language models.
explanation.why: Large language models break text into tokens, which can represent words, subwords, punctuation, or characters. The model processes and predicts text token by token during training and inference.
examples: "unbelievable" may be split into subword tokens
explanation.analogy: Tokens are like building blocks that AI models assemble into sentences.

options.text: Context window

explanation.summary: Context windows define how many tokens a model can process at once.
explanation.why: A context window refers to the maximum number of tokens an AI model can consider in a single interaction. It is related to token processing capacity, not the token units themselves.
explanation.keyDistinction: Context window measures token capacity, not token identity.

options.text: Embeddings

explanation.summary: Embeddings convert tokens into semantic numerical representations.
explanation.why: Embeddings are vectorized representations capturing semantic meaning and relationships between words or tokens. They are generated after tokenization and are not the original text units.
explanation.comparison: Tokens are raw text units, whereas embeddings are semantic encodings of those tokens.

questions.question: A shopping mall's AI security camera system disproportionately flags individuals from a specific ethnic group. Which type of bias is most likely responsible?

options.text: Measurement bias

explanation.summary: Measurement bias occurs from inaccurate data collection or labeling.
explanation.why: Measurement bias happens when collected data is systematically distorted due to faulty measurement processes or inconsistent labeling. While it can affect AI systems, disproportionate demographic misclassification is more commonly tied to unrepresentative datasets.

options.text: Sampling bias

explanation.summary: Sampling bias results from unrepresentative training data.
explanation.why: Sampling bias occurs when the training dataset does not adequately represent all demographic groups equally. In facial recognition or surveillance systems, underrepresentation of certain ethnic groups can cause higher error rates and disproportionate flagging.
keyPoints: Common issue in facial recognition systems
examples: Underrepresentation of darker skin tones in training datasets
explanation.comparison: Sampling bias affects dataset representation, whereas confirmation bias relates to human judgment.

options.text: Confirmation bias

explanation.summary: Confirmation bias reflects favoring preexisting beliefs or assumptions.
explanation.why: Confirmation bias is a cognitive bias where people interpret information in ways that confirm their existing beliefs. It is generally associated with human decision-making rather than dataset imbalance in AI models.

options.text: Observer bias

explanation.summary: Observer bias occurs when evaluators influence outcomes subjectively.
explanation.why: Observer bias happens when human interpretation or expectations influence observations or annotations. The scenario primarily points to biased training representation rather than subjective evaluation.

questions.question: A company deploys multiple ML models on Amazon SageMaker for real-time credit risk and fraud detection. Which SageMaker service can track and manage deployed models on endpoints?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth

explanation.summary: Ground Truth provides data labeling capabilities.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth is used to build labeled datasets for machine learning training using human annotators and automated labeling workflows.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

explanation.summary: JumpStart provides pre-trained models and ML templates.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart accelerates ML adoption by offering foundation models, notebooks, and solution templates, but it does not manage deployed model endpoints.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Clarify

explanation.summary: Clarify detects bias and explains model predictions.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Clarify helps evaluate fairness and explainability in ML models, but it is not designed for endpoint tracking or model inventory management.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Dashboard

explanation.summary: Model Dashboard tracks and manages deployed ML models.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Model Dashboard provides centralized visibility into deployed models, endpoints, monitoring status, metadata, and lifecycle management for ML governance and operational oversight.
examples: Monitoring fraud detection models in production

questions.question: A company is exploring Amazon Q to streamline business processes with automation and generative AI. Which generative AI techniques are used in Amazon Q Business? (Select two)

options.text: Diffusion Model

explanation.summary: Diffusion models are primarily used for image and media generation.
explanation.why: Diffusion models generate data such as images, audio, or video through iterative denoising processes. Amazon Q Business focuses on conversational enterprise AI rather than media generation.

options.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

explanation.summary: RAG combines retrieved enterprise data with generative AI responses.
explanation.why: Amazon Q Business retrieves relevant organizational information from connected enterprise data sources and augments prompts before generating responses, which is a core characteristic of Retrieval-Augmented Generation.

options.text: Generative adversarial network (GAN)

explanation.summary: GANs are commonly used for synthetic media generation.
explanation.why: Generative Adversarial Networks are mainly used for generating synthetic images, videos, and related content. They are not the primary architecture behind Amazon Q Business.

options.text: Large Language Model (LLM)

explanation.summary: LLMs power conversational reasoning and text generation.
explanation.why: Amazon Q Business relies on large language models to understand prompts, summarize information, answer questions, and automate business workflows using natural language interactions.

questions.question: A retail company wants to exclude competitive brand names or sensitive topics from generative AI content. What type of prompting technique does this represent?

options.text: Negative prompting

explanation.summary: Negative prompting instructs the model on what content to avoid.
explanation.why: Negative prompting explicitly tells the model not to include specific words, topics, brands, or styles in generated output. This is commonly used for content safety, brand protection, and compliance controls.

options.text: Zero-shot Prompting

explanation.summary: Zero-shot prompting performs tasks without examples.
explanation.why: Zero-shot prompting asks the model to complete a task directly without providing demonstrations or examples. It does not specifically focus on excluding content.

options.text: Few-shot Prompting

explanation.summary: Few-shot prompting teaches tasks using examples.
explanation.why: Few-shot prompting provides sample input-output pairs to guide model behavior. It is intended for task learning rather than explicitly blocking topics or terms.

options.text: Chain-of-thought prompting

explanation.summary: Chain-of-thought prompting encourages step-by-step reasoning.
explanation.why: Chain-of-thought prompting improves reasoning by asking models to explain intermediate steps. It is unrelated to restricting sensitive content generation.

questions.question: A retail company wants to leverage pre-trained computer vision models with the flexibility to customize them for specific business needs. What do you suggest?

options.text: Amazon DeepRacer

explanation.summary: DeepRacer focuses on reinforcement learning education and racing.
explanation.why: Amazon DeepRacer is designed to teach reinforcement learning concepts through autonomous racing simulations and is unrelated to enterprise computer vision customization.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker

explanation.summary: SageMaker is a general ML platform rather than a specialized pre-trained CV service.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker supports building, training, and deploying custom ML models, including computer vision workloads. However, the question specifically emphasizes pre-trained computer vision models with business customization, which aligns more directly with Rekognition Custom Labels.
explanation.comparison: SageMaker offers full ML flexibility, while Rekognition provides managed pre-trained CV APIs with customization.

options.text: Amazon Textract

explanation.summary: Textract extracts text and structured data from documents.
explanation.why: Amazon Textract specializes in OCR and document data extraction, not general-purpose computer vision customization.

options.text: Amazon Rekognition

explanation.summary: Rekognition provides pre-trained computer vision with customization capabilities.
explanation.why: Amazon Rekognition offers managed image and video analysis services such as object detection, facial analysis, and content moderation. Rekognition Custom Labels enables businesses to customize models using their own labeled datasets.

questions.question: An admissions committee wants to detect the use of generative AI in application essays to ensure submissions reflect genuine work. What issue is the committee primarily addressing?

options.text: Plagiarism

explanation.summary: Plagiarism concerns originality and authentic authorship of content.
explanation.why: The committee wants to ensure essays genuinely reflect applicants' own work rather than AI-generated or copied content. This aligns with concerns about originality, authorship integrity, and plagiarism.
explanation.comparison: Hallucination concerns factual accuracy, whereas plagiarism concerns authorship authenticity.

options.text: Bias

explanation.summary: Bias relates to unfair or skewed AI outcomes.
explanation.why: Bias refers to discriminatory or unfair patterns in AI systems and datasets, which is not the primary concern in evaluating essay originality.

options.text: Misinterpretation

explanation.summary: Misinterpretation refers to misunderstanding information or intent.
explanation.why: Misinterpretation involves incorrect understanding or analysis of information and does not directly relate to detecting AI-authored essays.

options.text: Hallucination

explanation.summary: Hallucination occurs when AI generates false or fabricated information.
explanation.why: Hallucinations involve inaccurate or invented responses generated by AI systems. The committee’s concern is authenticity and originality, not factual fabrication.

questions.question: A retail company wants to streamline ML workflows and improve collaboration. Which statement best defines the use of MLflow with Amazon SageMaker?

options.text: Manage machine learning experiments

explanation.summary: MLflow helps organize and track machine learning experiments.
explanation.why: MLflow with Amazon SageMaker enables teams to track experiments, log metrics, manage artifacts, compare runs, and collaborate across the machine learning lifecycle. It simplifies experiment management and improves reproducibility.

options.text: Leverage no-code ML

explanation.summary: No-code ML capabilities are associated with SageMaker Canvas.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Canvas enables users to build machine learning models without writing code. MLflow focuses on experiment tracking and lifecycle management rather than no-code development.
explanation.comparison: Canvas supports no-code ML, whereas MLflow supports experiment management.

options.text: Label data using human-in-the-loop

explanation.summary: Human-in-the-loop labeling is handled by SageMaker Ground Truth.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth provides managed workflows for data annotation and labeling using human reviewers and automated assistance. MLflow does not provide labeling capabilities.

options.text: Perform automatic model tuning

explanation.summary: Automatic model tuning optimizes hyperparameters rather than managing experiments.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning helps identify optimal hyperparameter values for ML models. MLflow instead focuses on experiment tracking and lifecycle management.
explanation.keyDistinction: Hyperparameter optimization differs from experiment orchestration and tracking.

questions.question: A retail company needs to perform sentiment analysis for its customer service audio calls. Which AWS services would you recommend for this requirement?

options.text: Amazon Translate and Amazon Comprehend

explanation.summary: Translate converts languages but does not transcribe speech audio.
explanation.why: Amazon Translate provides machine translation services, while Amazon Comprehend analyzes text sentiment. Since the input is audio calls, transcription is first required.

options.text: Amazon Rekognition and Amazon Transcribe

explanation.summary: Rekognition analyzes images and video rather than text sentiment.
explanation.why: Amazon Rekognition specializes in computer vision tasks such as object and facial recognition. It does not perform sentiment analysis on customer conversations.

options.text: Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Translate

explanation.summary: Translation services do not provide sentiment analysis.
explanation.why: Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text and Amazon Translate converts text between languages. Neither service analyzes sentiment directly.

options.text: Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Comprehend

explanation.summary: Transcribe converts audio to text and Comprehend analyzes sentiment.
explanation.why: Amazon Transcribe converts customer service audio calls into text, and Amazon Comprehend performs natural language processing tasks such as sentiment analysis on the transcribed conversations.
examples: Detecting negative customer sentiment in support calls

questions.question: A manufacturing company wants to use Amazon Bedrock to automate monitoring of inventory, sales, and supply chain data, and recommend reorder points. What do you recommend?

options.text: Watermark detection for Amazon Bedrock

explanation.summary: Watermark detection identifies AI-generated content authenticity.
explanation.why: Watermark detection focuses on identifying generated content and does not automate operational workflows or recommendations.

options.text: Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock

explanation.summary: Knowledge Bases improve retrieval of enterprise information.
explanation.why: Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock provide retrieval-augmented generation by connecting enterprise data sources, but they do not independently orchestrate automated actions or workflow decisions.
explanation.comparison: Knowledge Bases retrieve information, whereas agents automate actions and workflows.

options.text: Agents for Amazon Bedrock

explanation.summary: Agents automate workflows and orchestrate business tasks using AI.
explanation.why: Agents for Amazon Bedrock can coordinate multi-step workflows, retrieve operational data, make decisions, and automate actions such as monitoring inventory and recommending reorder points.
examples: Automatically generating reorder recommendations from inventory trends

options.text: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock

explanation.summary: Guardrails enforce safety and content controls for generative AI.
explanation.why: Guardrails help filter harmful or restricted outputs and enforce responsible AI policies. They do not automate operational monitoring or recommendations.

questions.question: A security company is evaluating Amazon Rekognition. Which of the following use cases is NOT the right fit for Amazon Rekognition?

options.text: Face-based user identity verification

explanation.summary: Rekognition supports facial analysis and identity verification.
explanation.why: Amazon Rekognition provides facial recognition and verification capabilities suitable for identity validation and authentication workflows.

options.text: Enable multilingual user experiences in your applications

options.text: Celebrity recognition

explanation.summary: Rekognition supports celebrity detection in images and videos.
explanation.why: Amazon Rekognition includes built-in celebrity recognition capabilities that can identify known public figures in visual content.

options.text: Searchable media libraries

explanation.summary: Rekognition can index and search image and video content.
explanation.why: Amazon Rekognition enables metadata extraction and indexing for visual content, making media assets searchable by detected labels or faces.

questions.question: A company is using generative AI to create custom reports. What are the key constituents of a good prompting technique for guiding the model to produce high-quality outputs?

options.text: Instructions, Hyperparameters, Input data, Output indicator

explanation.summary: Hyperparameters are model settings rather than core prompt constituents.
explanation.why: Prompt engineering focuses on instructions, context, input data, and expected output formatting. Hyperparameters such as temperature influence generation behavior but are not core prompt structure components.

options.text: Hyperparameters, Context, Input data, Output Indicator

explanation.summary: Good prompts require explicit instructions in addition to context.
explanation.why: Instructions tell the model what task to perform, making them a critical component of effective prompts. Hyperparameters alone do not replace clear instructions.

options.text: Instructions, Parameters, Input data, Output Indicator

explanation.summary: Context is a key prompt component for high-quality responses.
explanation.why: Providing context helps the model understand the background, domain, or constraints of the task. Generic parameters are less important than contextual guidance.
explanation.comparison: Context improves relevance, whereas parameters primarily influence generation style.

options.text: Instructions, Context, Input data, Output Indicator

explanation.summary: Effective prompts combine instructions, context, input data, and expected outputs.
explanation.why: High-quality prompts clearly define the task through instructions, provide contextual background, include the necessary input data, and specify the desired output format or indicator.
examples: Summarize this sales report in bullet points with a professional tone

questions.question: An e-commerce company is considering Amazon Personalize for tailored experiences based on user behavior. Which statement best describes Amazon Personalize?

options.text: Automatically convert speech to text and gain insights

explanation.summary: Speech-to-text functionality is provided by Amazon Transcribe.
explanation.why: Amazon Transcribe converts spoken language into text and supports analytics workflows, but it does not deliver personalized recommendations.

options.text: Derive and understand valuable insights from text within documents

explanation.summary: Text analysis capabilities are associated with Amazon Comprehend.
explanation.why: Amazon Comprehend performs NLP tasks such as sentiment analysis and entity recognition, but it is not a recommendation engine.

options.text: Deploy high-quality, natural-sounding human voices in dozens of languages

explanation.summary: Natural-sounding voice synthesis is provided by Amazon Polly.
explanation.why: Amazon Polly converts text into lifelike speech across multiple languages and voices. It does not personalize customer recommendations.

options.text: Elevate the customer experience with ML-powered personalization

explanation.summary: Amazon Personalize delivers ML-powered recommendation experiences.
explanation.why: Amazon Personalize uses machine learning to generate personalized recommendations, product suggestions, and tailored user experiences based on customer behavior and interaction history.

questions.question: A retail company wants to quickly get started with pre-built ML models and workflows. Which represent the key features of Amazon SageMaker JumpStart? (Select two)

options.text: You can build highly accurate ML models using a visual interface without any code

explanation.summary: No-code model building is primarily associated with SageMaker Canvas.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker Canvas enables users to build machine learning models through a visual no-code interface. SageMaker JumpStart instead focuses on pre-trained models, solution templates, and foundation model deployment.
explanation.comparison: Canvas targets no-code ML, whereas JumpStart accelerates pre-built ML adoption.

options.text: Pre-trained models are fully customizable for your use case with your data

explanation.summary: JumpStart provides customizable pre-trained models and workflows.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart offers pre-trained models and foundation models that can be fine-tuned or customized using organization-specific datasets for specialized business use cases.
examples: Customizing a text classification model for retail support tickets

options.text: Your inference and training data will be used to train the base model

explanation.summary: Customer inference data is not automatically used to retrain base foundation models.
explanation.why: AWS does not automatically use customer prompts or inference data to retrain shared foundation models in SageMaker JumpStart or Amazon Bedrock managed services.
explanation.keyDistinction: Customer data privacy is maintained unless explicitly configured for training workflows.

options.text: You can evaluate, compare, and select Foundation Models quickly based on pre-defined quality and responsibility metrics

explanation.summary: JumpStart supports evaluation and comparison of foundation models.
explanation.why: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart helps users evaluate and compare foundation models using predefined metrics such as quality, accuracy, and responsible AI considerations before selecting models for deployment.

questions.question: Which of the following are correct statements regarding AWS Global Infrastructure? (Select two)

options.text: Each AWS Region consists of a minimum of two Availability Zones (AZ)

explanation.summary: AWS Regions are generally designed with three or more Availability Zones.
explanation.why: Modern AWS Regions are architected to include multiple isolated Availability Zones, with most regions containing at least three AZs to support resilience and high availability.

options.text: Each AWS Region consists of a minimum of three Availability Zones (AZ)

explanation.summary: AWS Regions are built using multiple isolated Availability Zones.
explanation.why: AWS Regions are designed with multiple Availability Zones to improve fault tolerance, resilience, and high availability for customer workloads.

options.text: Each Availability Zone (AZ) consists of two or more discrete data centers

explanation.summary: Availability Zones can contain one or more data centers.
explanation.why: AWS defines an Availability Zone as one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity. The statement incorrectly enforces a minimum of two.
explanation.comparison: AWS documentation specifies one or more data centers, not necessarily two or more.

options.text: Each Availability Zone (AZ) consists of one or more discrete data centers

explanation.summary: Availability Zones contain one or more isolated data centers.
explanation.why: Each AWS Availability Zone is composed of one or more discrete physical data centers with independent infrastructure such as power, networking, and cooling.

questions.question: A company is deploying a generative AI model on Amazon Bedrock and needs to reduce the cost of usage while using prompt examples of up to 10 sample tasks as part of each input. Which approach would be the most effective in minimizing the costs associated with model usage?

options.text: The company should reduce the number of tokens in the input

explanation.summary: Reducing token usage directly lowers Bedrock inference costs.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock pricing is heavily based on the number of input and output tokens processed by foundation models. Few-shot prompting with many examples increases token consumption, so minimizing unnecessary prompt tokens is the most effective way to reduce inference costs.
explanation.performanceImpact: Lower token usage reduces inference latency and operational cost.

options.text: The company should reduce the top-P inference parameter for the model

explanation.summary: Top-P controls token selection diversity rather than usage cost.
explanation.why: Top-P (nucleus sampling) affects how candidate tokens are selected during generation, influencing creativity and variability, but it does not significantly reduce token processing costs.

options.text: The company should reduce the batch size while training the model

explanation.summary: Batch size is related to model training rather than Bedrock inference prompts.
explanation.why: The scenario concerns inference-time prompt usage on Amazon Bedrock, not custom model training workflows. Batch size impacts training efficiency but not prompt inference token costs.

options.text: The company should reduce the temperature inference parameter for the model

explanation.summary: Temperature affects randomness rather than token consumption.
explanation.why: Temperature changes the creativity and randomness of generated outputs, but it does not directly minimize the number of tokens processed or the overall inference cost.

questions.question: A company is using Amazon Bedrock and adjusting the Top P inference parameter. How does Top P influence the model response?

options.text: Specifies the sequences of characters that stop the model from generating further tokens

explanation.summary: Stop sequences control generation termination conditions.
explanation.why: Stop sequences instruct the model to stop generating output when specific tokens or phrases appear. This parameter is unrelated to Top-P sampling behavior.

options.text: Influences the number of most-likely candidates that the model considers for the next token

explanation.summary: Top-K controls the number of candidate tokens considered.
explanation.why: Top-K sampling limits the model to a fixed number of highest-probability candidate tokens, whereas Top-P uses cumulative probability thresholds.
explanation.comparison: Top-K uses fixed candidate counts, while Top-P uses cumulative probability percentages.

options.text: Influences the percentage of most-likely candidates that the model considers for the next token

explanation.summary: Top-P selects tokens based on cumulative probability thresholds.
explanation.why: Top-P, also called nucleus sampling, dynamically selects from the smallest set of candidate tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds the configured threshold P.
examples: P = 0.9 selects tokens contributing to the top 90% probability mass

options.text: Influences the likelihood of the model selecting lower-probability outputs, thereby impacting the creativity of the model's output

explanation.summary: Temperature controls randomness and creativity in outputs.
explanation.why: Temperature affects how likely the model is to choose lower-probability tokens, influencing output creativity and determinism. This behavior is separate from Top-P nucleus sampling.

questions.question: The marketing department at a media company wants to leverage Amazon Bedrock for making creative scripts for an upcoming ad campaign. What do you recommend?

options.text: Use higher Top-P to get more creative responses for the same prompt on Amazon Bedrock

explanation.summary: Top-P influences candidate selection but is not the primary creativity control.
explanation.why: While increasing Top-P can slightly broaden the candidate token pool, temperature is the more direct and commonly recommended parameter for increasing creativity and variability in generated outputs.

options.text: Use lower Top-P to get more creative responses for the same prompt on Amazon Bedrock

explanation.summary: Lower Top-P reduces diversity and makes outputs more conservative.
explanation.why: Reducing Top-P narrows the candidate token pool, making model responses more deterministic and less creative.

options.text: Use lower Temperature to get more creative responses for the same prompt on Amazon Bedrock

explanation.summary: Lower temperature produces more predictable and deterministic outputs.
explanation.why: Lower temperature reduces randomness, causing the model to prefer high-probability tokens and generate safer, less diverse responses.
explanation.comparison: Higher temperature increases creativity, while lower temperature increases consistency.

options.text: Use higher Temperature to get more creative responses for the same prompt on Amazon Bedrock

explanation.summary: Higher temperature increases creativity and response diversity.
explanation.why: Increasing the temperature parameter allows the model to sample lower-probability tokens more frequently, producing more varied, imaginative, and creative outputs suitable for marketing and advertising content generation.
examples: Generating varied advertising slogans and campaign scripts

questions.question: A healthcare company has fine-tuned a foundation model in Amazon Bedrock using a task-specific labeled dataset of clinical notes. What is required to deploy and run inference on this custom model?

options.text: The company should leverage batch inference to facilitate fine-tuning of the model

explanation.summary: Batch inference processes large datasets but does not reserve deployment capacity.
explanation.why: Batch inference is designed for offline large-scale prediction workloads and is unrelated to provisioning throughput capacity for serving a custom fine-tuned model in Amazon Bedrock.

options.text: The company should use On-Demand mode, which provides flexibility by charging only for the resources consumed

explanation.summary: Custom fine-tuned Bedrock models require provisioned throughput for inference.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock custom models require Provisioned Throughput to deploy and perform inference. On-demand inference applies to supported base foundation models, not custom fine-tuned deployments.
explanation.comparison: On-demand is suitable for shared base models, whereas Provisioned Throughput is required for custom models.

options.text: The company should leverage Amazon Bedrock playground to facilitate fine-tuning of the model

explanation.summary: The Bedrock playground is used for testing prompts and models.
explanation.why: The playground environment supports experimentation and prompt testing but is not a deployment requirement for serving fine-tuned models in production.

options.text: The company should use Provisioned Throughput mode, which allows the company to reserve a specific amount of capacity in advance

explanation.summary: Provisioned Throughput reserves dedicated capacity for custom Bedrock models.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock requires Provisioned Throughput for deploying and running inference on fine-tuned custom foundation models. This reserves dedicated model capacity and ensures predictable performance.

questions.question: A company fine-tuned a Foundation Model on Amazon Bedrock using training data that includes confidential information. How can the company ensure the model's responses do not contain this confidential information?

options.text: The company should mask the confidential information from the model responses by leveraging Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

explanation.summary: Bedrock Guardrails can filter and mask sensitive information in responses.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails support sensitive information filtering and content controls that help prevent confidential data from appearing in generated outputs.
examples: Blocking disclosure of patient identifiers in clinical responses

options.text: The company should use encryption to protect the confidential information in the model responses

explanation.summary: Encryption protects stored or transmitted data but not generated output disclosure.
explanation.why: Encryption secures data at rest and in transit, but it does not prevent the model from generating confidential information during inference.

options.text: The company should delete the customized model, remove confidential information from the training data, and fine-tune the model again

explanation.summary: Retraining is disruptive and not the intended Bedrock response-control mechanism.
explanation.why: Although retraining without sensitive data could reduce memorization risks, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails are specifically designed to filter and block confidential information in outputs without rebuilding the model.
explanation.comparison: Guardrails provide runtime protection, whereas retraining requires rebuilding the model lifecycle.

options.text: The company should swap Amazon Bedrock with Amazon SageMaker and rebuild the model using Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithms

explanation.summary: Switching platforms does not inherently solve confidential output exposure.
explanation.why: The issue concerns output governance and sensitive data filtering rather than the ML platform itself.

questions.question: What is a key difference between Foundation Models (FMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) in the context of generative AI?

options.text: Large Language Models are pre-trained on massive datasets and can be fine-tuned for specific tasks, whereas Foundation Models are not pre-trained and are built from scratch for each application

explanation.summary: Foundation Models are also pre-trained models.
explanation.why: Foundation Models are large pre-trained models designed for broad adaptability across tasks and domains. They are not built from scratch for every application.

options.text: Foundation Models are specifically designed for text generation, while Large Language Models can generate images, videos, and audio

explanation.summary: LLMs are specialized for language tasks rather than multimodal generation.
explanation.why: Large Language Models focus primarily on language understanding and generation. Foundation Models can include text, image, audio, or multimodal systems.
explanation.comparison: LLMs are a subset of Foundation Models specialized for language.

options.text: Foundation Models serve as a broad base for various AI applications by providing generalized capabilities, whereas Large Language Models are specialized for understanding and generating human language

explanation.summary: Foundation Models are generalized models, while LLMs focus on language tasks.
explanation.why: Foundation Models provide adaptable capabilities across domains and modalities, whereas Large Language Models specifically focus on natural language understanding and generation.
keyPoints: LLMs are a subset of Foundation Models
Foundation Models can support multimodal tasks

options.text: Foundation Models are only used in academic research, while Large Language Models are used in commercial applications

explanation.summary: Foundation Models are widely used in commercial AI applications.
explanation.why: Foundation Models are broadly deployed across enterprise and commercial AI workloads, including Amazon Bedrock services.

questions.question: A company is comparing Amazon Q and Amazon Bedrock for AI-driven tasks. Which statements correctly describe the differences? (Select two)

options.text: With Amazon Q, you can choose the underlying Foundation Model. However, Amazon Bedrock does not allow you to choose the underlying Foundation Model

explanation.summary: Amazon Bedrock provides model choice across multiple foundation models.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock allows customers to select from multiple foundation models offered by AWS and third-party providers, whereas Amazon Q abstracts the underlying model selection.

options.text: With Amazon Bedrock, you can choose the underlying Foundation Model. However, Amazon Q does not allow you to choose the underlying Foundation Model

explanation.summary: Bedrock provides foundation model choice while Amazon Q abstracts it.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock enables developers to select, customize, and integrate foundation models directly. Amazon Q is a managed generative AI assistant where the underlying model selection is abstracted from end users.
keyPoints: Amazon Q is managed assistant experience
Developers control model choice in Bedrock

options.text: Both Amazon Q and Amazon Bedrock are generative AI-powered assistants that allow you to create pre-packaged generative AI applications

explanation.summary: Amazon Bedrock is a development platform rather than a packaged assistant.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock provides infrastructure and APIs for building generative AI applications, while Amazon Q is a managed assistant experience.
explanation.comparison: Amazon Q is an assistant product, whereas Bedrock is a generative AI platform.

options.text: Amazon Q is a generative AI–powered assistant that allows you to create pre-packaged generative AI applications, whereas Amazon Bedrock provides an environment to build and scale generative AI applications using a Foundation Model (FM)

explanation.summary: Amazon Q provides assistant experiences while Bedrock enables custom AI application development.
explanation.why: Amazon Q delivers managed generative AI assistant capabilities for business productivity, whereas Amazon Bedrock provides APIs and tooling to build, customize, and scale generative AI applications using foundation models.

questions.question: A company builds generative AI solutions. Which option best summarizes the differences between model inference and model evaluation?

options.text: Both model inference and model evaluation refer to the process of a model generating an output (response) from a given input (prompt)

explanation.summary: Inference generates outputs while evaluation assesses model quality.
explanation.why: Model inference refers to generating predictions or responses from inputs, whereas model evaluation compares performance and suitability across tasks or metrics.

options.text: Both model inference and model evaluation refer to the process of evaluating and comparing model outputs to determine the model that is best suited for a use case

explanation.summary: Evaluation compares models, whereas inference generates responses.

questions.question: An e-commerce chatbot on Amazon Bedrock should continuously learn and improve from real-time customer interactions. Which approach is most suitable for enabling ongoing self-improvement?

questions.question: A company is building a RAG-based customer support solution on Amazon Bedrock. Which database solution is most appropriate for fast index lookups and similarity searches?

options.text: Amazon DynamoDB

explanation.summary: DynamoDB is optimized for key-value and document workloads rather than vector similarity search.
explanation.why: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database designed for low-latency key-value and document access patterns. While highly scalable, it is not purpose-built for vector embeddings or semantic similarity searches used in RAG systems.
explanation.comparison: DynamoDB supports fast transactional lookups, whereas OpenSearch supports vector and semantic search.

options.text: Amazon Aurora

explanation.summary: Aurora is a relational database service rather than a vector search engine.
explanation.why: Amazon Aurora is optimized for relational workloads and transactional SQL queries. Although extensions can support advanced search capabilities, it is not the primary AWS service for large-scale vector similarity search in RAG architectures.

options.text: Amazon OpenSearch Service

explanation.summary: OpenSearch supports vector similarity search and high-performance indexing.
explanation.why: Amazon OpenSearch Service provides full-text search, indexing, and vector similarity search capabilities that are well-suited for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures. It enables efficient retrieval of semantically similar embeddings for generative AI applications.
examples: Retrieving semantically related support articles for customer queries
explanation.performanceImpact: Efficient vector indexing improves retrieval speed and response relevance in RAG pipelines.

options.text: Amazon DocumentDB

explanation.summary: DocumentDB is designed for document-oriented workloads rather than semantic vector search.
explanation.why: Amazon DocumentDB provides MongoDB-compatible document database functionality for JSON-style data storage and querying. It is not primarily designed for high-performance embedding similarity search used in RAG systems.
